statement: The function returns a result r, and r contains exactly the stable mountain indices, each exactly once, in some order: for every integer v, the number of positions j with 0 <= j < len(r) and r[j] = v equals 1 if (1 <= v <= len(height) - 1 and height[v - 1] > threshold), and equals 0 otherwise. (Equivalently, as a multiset r is exactly the set { i : 1 <= i < len(height) and height[i - 1] > threshold }.)
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(height) <= 100 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(height); threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.

statement: For every such height and threshold, the function returns a result r; it never fails (no arithmetic overflow, no out-of-bounds access, no panic).
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(height) <= 100 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(height); threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every element of r is a valid non-zero index of height: for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), 1 <= r[j] <= len(height) - 1. In particular, 0 never occurs in r and no index >= len(height) occurs in r.
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(height) <= 100 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(height); threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every returned index is a valid stable mountain: for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), 1 <= r[j] < len(height) and height[r[j] - 1] > threshold.
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(height) <= 100 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(height); threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every stable mountain index is present in r: for every i with 1 <= i < len(height), if height[i - 1] > threshold then there exists j with 0 <= j < len(r) and r[j] = i.
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(height) <= 100 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(height); threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r has no repeated elements: for all j and k with 0 <= j < k < len(r), r[j] != r[k].
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(height) <= 100 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(height); threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the length of r equals the number of stable mountains: len(r) = the number of indices i with 1 <= i < len(height) and height[i - 1] > threshold.
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(height) <= 100 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(height); threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and len(height) = 2, the answer is determined by the single candidate mountain 1: if height[0] > threshold then len(r) = 1 and r[0] = 1; if height[0] <= threshold then len(r) = 0.
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with len(height) = 2 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for i with 0 <= i < 2; threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) >= 1 if and only if there exists an index i with 1 <= i < len(height) and height[i - 1] > threshold.
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(height) <= 100 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(height); threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.

statement: Let r1 be the result of calling the function on (height, t1) and r2 the result on (height, t2) (both exist by no-failure). Then every index returned for the larger threshold is also returned for the smaller threshold: for every j with 0 <= j < len(r2) there exists k with 0 <= k < len(r1) and r1[k] = r2[j].
preconditions: height is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(height) <= 100 and 1 <= height[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(height); t1 and t2 are 64-bit integers with 1 <= t1 <= t2 <= 100.

statement: Suppose that for every i with 0 <= i < n - 1, (height1[i] > t1) holds if and only if (height2[i] > t2) holds. Let r1, r2 be the results on (height1, t1) and (height2, t2) respectively (both exist by no-failure). Then r1 and r2 contain the same multiset of indices: for every integer v, the number of positions j with r1[j] = v equals the number of positions j with r2[j] = v.
preconditions: height1 and height2 are slices of 64-bit integers with len(height1) = len(height2) = n, 2 <= n <= 100, and all entries of both in the range [1, 100]; t1 and t2 are 64-bit integers with 1 <= t1 <= 100 and 1 <= t2 <= 100.

statement: Let r1 be the result on (height1, threshold) and r2 the result on (height2, threshold) (both exist by no-failure). Then every index returned for height1 is also returned for height2: for every j with 0 <= j < len(r1) there exists k with 0 <= k < len(r2) and r2[k] = r1[j].
preconditions: height1 and height2 are slices of 64-bit integers with len(height1) = len(height2) = n, 2 <= n <= 100, all entries in [1, 100], and height1[i] <= height2[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n; threshold is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= threshold <= 100.
